title: Placeus, Vermigli, Musculus: essential act is practical assent — especially to Gospel promises
source_text: LXXX. Itaque si quis quaerat quis sit proprius & essentialis fidei salvificae actus, secundum mentem Doctorum illorum respondendum est, hunc actum esse assensum practicum toti Verbo Dei adhibitum, sed speciatim promissionibus Evangelii. Quae sententia est Josuae Placei in Thesibus Salmuriensibus, ubi ut supra vidimus, fides ab eo definitur, Tenax & efficax persuasio veritatis eorum quae Verbo Dei nobis revelata sunt, speciatim vero promissionis de remissione peccatorum, & vita aeterna nobis per Christum parta. Et Petri quoque Martyris, cui fides est assensus praebitus Verbo Dei, qui tantarum sit virium & efficaciae, ut trahat secum affectum fiduciae, spei, charitatis, & omnia tandem bona opera, ut praesentis vitae infirmitas patitur. Denique Wolfgangi Musculi, qui fidem definit, Consensum assensum cordis ad ea quae vel narrantur, vel promittuntur Verbo.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore if anyone asks what is the proper and essential act of saving faith, according to the mind of those Doctors it is to be answered that this act is a practical assent applied to the whole Word of God, but specially to the promises of the Gospel. Which is the opinion of Joshua de la Place in the Salmurian Theses, where as we saw above, faith is defined by him as A tenacious and efficacious persuasion of the truth of those things which have been revealed to us by the Word of God, but specially of the promise of the remission of sins and eternal life procured for us through Christ. And also of Peter Martyr, for whom faith is an assent given to the Word of God, of such strength and efficacy that it draws with it the affection of trust, of hope, of charity, and at length all good works, as the infirmity of the present life allows. Finally of Wolfgang Musculus, who defines faith as A consenting assent of the heart to those things which are either narrated or promised by the Word.
pass_b_english: On that line, saving faith’s proper essential act = practical assent to the whole Word, specially to Gospel promises.
Placeus (Saumur): tenacious, efficacious persuasion of what God reveals — specially remission and eternal life through Christ.
Vermigli: assent so strong it draws fiducia, hope, charity, and good works as present weakness allows.
Musculus: consenting heart-assent to what the Word narrates or promises.
